H-E1 data loader filters real MBPP task IDs and asserts exactly 500 problems, indicating benchmark-backed evaluation rather than synthetic generation (2026_verifai__h-e1__code__data.py:17-18, 30).
H-E1 execution log shows an actual run on MBPP: 'Dataset: mbpp (IDs 11-510)', then '[1/6] Loading MBPP test set...' and 'Loaded 500 problems' (2026_verifai__h-e1__code__experiment.log:7, 11-12).

Saved H-E1 results contain per-task outputs from that run, e.g. task_id 11 with runtime_error metadata in execution_results.json, confirming experiment artifacts were produced from benchmark tasks (2026_verifai__h-e1__code__results__execution_results.json pattern: first record has task_id 11, category runtime_error).

H-M1 repair code reuses H-E1 execution results and also reloads the MBPP test split with load_dataset("mbpp", split="test") to build the repair dataset index (2026_verifai__h-m1__code__data.py:21-29, 43-55).

H-M1 execution log confirms actual benchmark-backed repair runs: 304 runtime cases loaded from H-E1, 500 MBPP tasks loaded, and 1,520 repair attempts executed (2026_verifai__h-m1__code__experiment.log:13-19, 27-31).

Downstream H-M2/H-M3 analyses consume H-M1 result files rather than any synthetic dataset generator, so the paper-level experiments remain grounded in prior MBPP runs (2026_verifai__h-m2__code__run_experiment.py:64-71; 2026_verifai__h-m3__code__train.py:36, 41).

Repository-wide search under experiments/ found no synthetic-data indicators such as np.random, SyntheticDataset, torch.randn, Simulator, or Mock, reducing evidence for a synthetic or fabricated setup.
